## Before the first half

Nothing new. Both of day 5's reproductions run on what you already have: numpy,
sympy and matplotlib, plus `pycbc` for three published noise curves, which you
have had since day 2.

`et-ce-horizon` deliberately **imports** day 2's matched-filter module rather
than restating any of it. That module is in the repository, not in your copy. The import searches for it; if you have moved things around it will
tell you where it looked.

---

## Before the second half

A terminal and a working agent, as on every other day, and one thing more:
`day5/exercise/` is the scaffold the session's launch task runs in — one task,
three directories, and the only difference between them is what sits in the
directory before the agent starts. Copy it somewhere of your own before the
hour and read its `README.md`, which is short. If you use Codex, the hooks in
`b/` and `c/` have to be trusted in `/hooks` before they will run.

The paper the task points at is `day1/papers/PhysRev.136.B1224.pdf`, which
you have had since the first morning. Nothing else is needed, and nothing is
downloaded.

## The numbers the day turns on

| | |
|---|---|
| GW170817's lag to the gamma-ray burst | **1.74 s**, over a light travel time of $8.5\times10^{7}$ yr |
| the fractional speed difference | $-3.1\times10^{-15} < \Delta v/v < +6.5\times10^{-16}$, reproducing the published $[-3\times10^{-15}, +7\times10^{-16}]$ |
| the distance the paper uses | **26 Mpc**, the 90 % *lower* bound — not the 40 Mpc everyone quotes |
| what the exotic emission window costs | a factor of **121** on the lower bound, and the paper says so itself |
| Advanced LIGO at design, for a 36 + 29 binary | **4511 Mpc** at $\rho = 8$ |
| the Einstein Telescope, and Cosmic Explorer | **×16.8** and **×53.0** in distance; **×4.7×10³** and **×1.5×10⁵** in Euclidean volume |
| at 100 Hz, in amplitude | **×10.1** and **×25.1** — the horizon ratios are larger because the low-frequency wall moves too |
| the heaviest binary in band at all | **440** solar masses at a 10 Hz wall, **879** at 5 Hz |
| where Euclidean stops meaning anything | $c/H_0 = $ **4428 Mpc**, which both 3G horizons run past |

Every one has a check behind it and a figure you can open. The two
reproductions carry **26 checks** between them; `day5-all-figures.html` shows
both figures beside the code that made them.

---

## Scope

**Today is pointers.** Four topics in the lecture, each stated rather than
derived, and nothing derived that days 1–4 do not already derive. If you want
the derivation, it is in the earlier day.

Two figures, where day 3 had fifteen. That is the design: almost everything on
today's slides is borrowed, with the credit printed on the slide and recorded in
the day's ledger. The two that are rendered are the two the lecture makes a
quantitative claim from.

The horizon figure is **Euclidean**, and past $c/H_0$ that is not an
approximation — it is not a distance at all, because the mass in band is not the
mass at the source. The figure says so on its face, and doing it properly — with
redshift in, so the mass in band is not the mass at the source — is a good week's
work.

---

## The point of the day

The course opened more than it closed, and the lecture ends on the questions
rather than on a summary.

What you take home is `homework.html`. Each exercise on it runs one task more
than once and changes a single thing about how the agent is run. The physics
under them is interchangeable, and the last one only works on something of your
own.
